blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the intermediate level, it helps to stop thinking of tax as a bill and start thinking of it as a relationship. Every year, a company and the tax authority exchange information, payments, clarifications, and occasionally disagreements. How the company behaves across those exchanges shapes how it is treated over the following years.

Companies that have been consistently honest, organised and responsive tend to find that their difficult years are easier. The authority assumes good faith, gives reasonable time, and often accepts small corrections without penalty. Companies that have been inconsistent find the opposite — small issues become formal investigations, and reasonable time disappears.

The relationship is built on small daily choices: a clean return filed on time, a quick answer to a question, a voluntary correction when a mistake is found. None of this is dramatic, and all of it compounds quietly over years into real protection when something eventually goes wrong.

items.q: According to the text, how should a company at this level think about tax?
options: As a problem for the finance team only
As a relationship, not just a bill
As something to postpone whenever possible
items.why: "stop thinking of tax as a bill and start thinking of it as a relationship."

items.q: What do consistently honest and responsive companies tend to experience?
options: Easier difficult years and assumed good faith
No contact with the authority at all
items.why: "their difficult years are easier. The authority assumes good faith, gives reasonable time…"

items.q: What is the relationship built on, according to the text?
options: Small daily choices that compound over time
items.why: "The relationship is built on small daily choices… all of it compounds quietly over years."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: How a company behaves this year affects future years.
A voluntary correction can protect a company later.
Protection can be bought quickly once a crisis begins.
Good faith is earned through consistent behaviour.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a proteção é construída quietly over years — não se compra na hora da crise.

items.q: The phrase "reasonable time disappears" for inconsistent companies suggests that…
options: they no longer need to file returns
their deadlines are legally shorter than others'
the authority pressures them harder when problems arise
items.why: Inferência: perdida a boa-fé, small issues become formal investigations e a margem de tolerância some.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando a um novo diretor. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, you asked why that error last month didn't turn into a nightmare. Honestly, it comes down to something that started long before either of us was here.

For years, this company has filed clean returns on time. When we've spotted a small mistake, we've corrected it ourselves before anyone asked. And when the tax office has sent a question, we've answered within days, not weeks. None of that felt important at the time — it was just good housekeeping.

Then last month we underpaid by a small amount because of a system glitch. With another company, that could have triggered a full investigation. Instead, the officer called, we explained, we paid, and it was closed in a week. She assumed we'd made an honest mistake — because for ten years, that's exactly what the record showed.

That's the point I want you to take away. We didn't buy that outcome last month. We earned it, quietly, over a decade of boring, consistent behaviour. So please, keep the returns clean, keep answering fast. You won't see the value most years. You'll see it on the one year it really matters.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is James explaining all of this to the new director?
options: To justify raising the tax budget
To announce a new tax strategy
To criticise the finance team's work
To explain why last month's error did not become a big problem
items.why: "you asked why that error last month didn't turn into a nightmare."

items.q: What has the company consistently done over the years?
options: Delayed payments to improve cash flow
Avoided contact with the tax office
Filed clean returns on time and corrected mistakes itself
items.why: "filed clean returns on time… we've corrected it ourselves before anyone asked."

items.q: How was last month's underpayment resolved?
options: It led to a full investigation
It resulted in a large penalty
It was closed within a week after a call and payment
It was ignored by the authority
items.why: "the officer called, we explained, we paid, and it was closed in a week."

items.q: When James says "We didn't buy that outcome last month. We earned it," he means that…
options: the company paid extra to avoid the investigation
the good result came from years of consistent behaviour, not a quick fix
the error was never actually reported
the officer was a personal friend
items.why: Inferência: a proteção foi construída ao longo de dez anos, não comprada no momento da crise.

items.q: What does James imply with "You won't see the value most years"?
options: The tax office rarely checks returns
The consistent effort is a waste of time
The benefit is invisible until a rare, difficult moment arrives
The director should reduce contact with the authority
items.why: Inferência: o valor da boa-fé só aparece no ano em que algo dá errado — por isso vale manter a consistência.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We sent a clarification to explain how the figure was calculated." A clarification is…
options: an explanation that makes something clearer
items.why: Clarification = esclarecimento: algo que torna a informação mais clara.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The authority assumed we were acting in ___ and gave us time to fix the error."
items.why: Good faith = boa-fé: a presunção de honestidade que facilita a tolerância da autoridade.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "When we found the mistake, we made a ___ before the audit even started."
items.why: Voluntary correction = correção voluntária: corrigir o erro por conta própria, sem ser cobrado.

items.q: "Small good habits compound over the years." To compound here means to…
options: build up and increase over time
items.why: To compound = compor-se, acumular efeito ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "The company behaved consistently across every filing." This means it acted…
options: in the same reliable way each time
items.why: Consistently = consistentemente: de forma estável e previsível, sempre do mesmo modo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre compliance e impostos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The director has to sign off on the annual return before we file it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We spotted the error and decided to come clean with the tax office." To come clean means to…
items.why: Come clean = assumir a verdade, admitir o erro em vez de escondê-lo.

items.q: "The team agreed to fix the process but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "One late filing won't move the needle on our overall record." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não muda o quadro geral.

items.q: "A clean track record helps you stay on top of your tax obligations." To stay on top of means to…
options: keep in control of and up to date with
items.why: Stay on top of = manter sob controle, acompanhar de perto sem deixar acumular.
